title: Post-1997 runoff losses in south-east Australia and the eastern US were not stored and did not come from rain-gauge noise; their forms differed at equal aridity (CAMELS, GRACE, 1951-2025)
abstract: Question: after 1997, runoff in south-east Australia (SE-AU) and in the eastern US fell below each catchment's 1951-1996 rainfall-runoff relation by about 40 mm per year. The SE-AU deficit is a loss of runoff response to rain, and the eastern US deficit is a constant offset. Where did the water go, and which mechanisms agree with each form? Approach: we used CAMELS-AUS v2.03 (1951-2021) and CAMELS-US with USGS flow (1951-2025) with four rain sources per continent, including fixed GHCN-Daily gauge networks, three PET products and CSR GRACE/GRACE-FO RL06.3 water storage. For five mechanisms (more evaporation for the same climate, higher PET, rain that reads high, a loss proportional to flow, a constant loss), the Fu form of the Budyko curve gave the expected ratio of slope change to offset. We compared each prediction with the observed slope change, with cluster-bootstrap intervals and a 35-window pre-1997 time null. Results: from 2010 to the end of the records, the cumulative runoff deficit was 484 mm in SE-AU (95% CI 282-700) and 538 mm in the eastern US (304-743), but GRACE storage rose by only 82 mm and 28 mm. Thus storage can hold at most 17% and 5% of the missing water. With fixed gauges the SE-AU slope loss was 25% (18-31%), and it was 22-26% with AGCD, SILO and CRU; all values were below all 35 time-null values. Rain-source disagreement did not increase, so rain-data noise does not explain the slope loss. The eastern US loss agreed with a constant loss (offset -7.0%, slope change -0.4%); a proportional loss and a rain overestimate were rejected by the bootstrap and had time-null p = 0.06-0.08. PET fell by 0.7% in 1997-2009 when the eastern US deficit started. In SE-AU, a constant loss and a Budyko-parameter change predicted too little slope loss (time-null p = 0.03); a proportional loss, higher PET or rain bias came closer, and the time null could not separate them. PET products disagreed (-0.3% to +5.9%) and explained 0-6% of a 20% flow loss. At the same aridity (PET/P about 0.85), SE-AU catchments lost 22% of the slope and eastern US catchments did not. Conclusion: the missing runoff in both regions left the catchments, most probably as evapotranspiration or water use, and the two regions had different changes, not one change seen through two climates. Limitations: evaporation is inferred, not measured; GRACE resolution is about 300 km; farm dams and vegetation were not tested directly.

display.caption: Cumulative runoff residual since 2003 and GRACE water-storage change at the same catchments. Storage did not rise by the missing runoff in south-east Australia or the eastern US.

Observed slope change and offset after 2009 with four rain sources, against the forms that five mechanisms predict. South-east Australia lies below the Budyko-family range; the eastern US lies on the constant-loss line.
The south-east Australian slope loss is the same with fixed gauge networks, and rain-source disagreement did not increase enough after 1997 to make it by noise.
